Splashery · Updated October 11, 2026

The Tinkerer's Manual

How to program Gaussian splats: what one splat is, how the toys are built, and a small language for writing your own splat equations, and toys that show pictures and read what you type.

Almost every toy in the Splashery Playground is made of Gaussian splats: tens of thousands of soft, colored blobs that blend into a solid-looking thing. This manual is for anyone who knows some math and wants to make splats do what they say. It goes chapter by chapter. You can stop after any chapter and still have something to play with.

Splashery is primarily splat based, but not only. Two honest exceptions. The photo toys (Photo to 3D and Moving photo to 3D) open in a Sharp view, a second way to see the same photo: the picture at its full resolution on a textured relief (a mesh of triangles) lifted by the same depth, so small text stays readable. That view is not drawn with splats; the splats are switched off while it shows. The Splats / Sharp switch in the toy's panel brings the splats back. And the liquids and flames are part splats and part something else: see "What else Splashery does now" for how each fluid is drawn. (The Studio toys are behind the labs switch; see the same chapter.)
